title: Lemon poppy-seed muffins
summary: Bright, tangy almond-flour muffins flecked with poppy seeds and brushed with a lemon glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk the almond flour, coconut flour, baking powder, salt, erythritol and poppy seeds.
Whisk the eggs, melted butter, sour cream, lemon zest, lemon juice and vanilla, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Divide between the cases and bake 20–22 minutes, until golden and springy.
Stir the powdered erythritol and lemon juice into a thin glaze and brush over the muffins while they are still warm. Cool 15 minutes in the tin.
dairy_free_notes: Coconut yogurt keeps them moist but slightly less tangy; add an extra teaspoon of lemon zest.
tips: Rub the zest into the erythritol first to release more lemon oil.

origin.history: Poppy seed is an old ingredient in Central and Eastern European baking. Paired with lemon in an American-style quick-bread muffin, it became a familiar bakery and coffee-shop flavour in the United States by the late 1900s.
